caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
raw_response:
The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of completions and coverage for four different language models. The x-axis is labeled "Number of completions (k)" and has a logarithmic scale, ranging from 2<sup>0</sup> to 2<sup>8</sup>, with tick labels at each power of 2. The y-axis is labeled "Coverage" and has a linear scale, ranging from 0.2 to 0.9, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. There are four data series represented as lines with markers. The "Llama-3B" series is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers; it starts at approximately 0.42 coverage at 2<sup>0</sup> and increases to approximately 0.92 coverage at 2<sup>8</sup>. The "Llama-3B + FT" series is represented by a dashed green line with square markers; it follows a similar trend to "Llama-3B", starting at approximately 0.43 coverage at 2<sup>0</sup> and reaching approximately 0.92 coverage at 2<sup>8</sup>. The "Llama-1B" series is represented by a solid light blue line with triangular markers; it begins at approximately 0.22 coverage at 2<sup>0</sup> and increases to approximately 0.72 coverage at 2<sup>6</sup>, with minimal change from 2<sup>6</sup> to 2<sup>8</sup>. Finally, the "Llama-1B + FT" series is represented by a dashed light green line with diamond markers; it starts at approximately 0.27 coverage at 2<sup>0</sup> and increases to approximately 0.77 coverage at 2<sup>8</sup>.
